SMTO-CFG-0054 — SMTO can't start because the Model's default temperature is negative

GUID: 47e6adb3-18a6-4abc-8999-88d79c7e9af8
Slug: config-default-temperature-must-be-zero-or-greater
Domain: CFG · Subsystem: cfg

What happened

  • SMTO stopped while starting because the Model's default temperature — a number that controls how varied its answers are — is below zero. Your conversations and settings were not changed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open the config.yaml file in the SMTO folder, or the file named after --config in the command that starts SMTO. Find the default_temperature: line under llm:. This default temperature comes from that line, and a temperature below zero isn't valid.
  2. Change it to 0.1, SMTO's usual value, or another number of zero or more. You can also delete the line to use 0.1. Lower numbers give steadier answers, and zero is allowed.
  3. Save the file, then select Start again on the startup screen, or start SMTO the way you normally do. SMTO reads config.yaml only when it starts.

What success looks like

  • The startup screen reaches Ready and the Model answers a new message.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who installed SMTO. Don't send config.yaml itself, because it can contain your Model access key, and don't change the Model's timeouts or token limits to clear this error.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Settings validation rejected default_temperature (config.yaml llm.default_temperature) because it is below zero.

What this means

  • default_temperature is below zero during application settings validation. Validation reports the owning configuration boundary; it does not change settings, migrate retained state or grant authority. Existing tasks retain their accepted snapshots unless the specific control explicitly supports a live change.

Why this can happen

  • default_temperature is below zero during application settings validation.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect default_temperature separately from the bounded llm_request_temperature override.

How to fix it

  • Set llm.default_temperature in the bootstrap config.yaml (or the file named by AOR_APP_CONFIG_PATH or --config) to a value of 0 or more (default 0.1), or remove it, and restart the Server. It is the client fallback temperature passed to build_openai_compatible_llm_client and is separate from llm_request_temperature (0 to 1) and the temperature in a Model routing profile's parameters.
  • Set default_temperature to a supported nonnegative value for the selected model.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The configured nonnegative default passes its owning validation.

What not to do

  • Do not change an unrelated timeout, budget or policy. Check whether the named setting applies only to a new task.

Technical notes

  • Validation reports the owning configuration boundary; it does not change settings, migrate retained state or grant authority. Existing tasks retain their accepted snapshots unless the specific control explicitly supports a live change.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
